additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

info.persona: Patricia Horney is a curiosity‑driven marketing leader who balances a voracious appetite for art, food, and adventure with a lingering propensity for stress‑induced worry, making them both the life of any gathering and a relentless self‑improver.
info.professional_persona: Patricia Horney leverages her strategic marketing expertise—spanning integrated brand narratives, data‑driven digital campaigns, SEO/SEM, and emerging AR/VR experiences—while they channel her curiosity and sociable flair into leading cross‑functional teams, championing purpose‑driven storytelling, and thriving as the vibrant center of brainstorming sessions.
info.cultural_background: Patricia was raised in a middle‑class, Anglo‑American family in suburban Texas and has spent her adult life in Austin. Her upbringing combined the warm hospitality of traditional Southern culture with the progressive, eclectic spirit of the city’s music, art, and tech scenes. A liberal arts education reinforced her appreciation for diverse perspectives, while her professional experience in the vibrant Austin market has immersed her in a culture that values creativity, collaboration, and entrepreneurial risk‑taking. She identifies with a blend of classic Texan values—community, independence, and modesty—and a forward‑looking, inclusive ethos shaped by the city’s multicultural environment.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Patricia’s curiosity fuels a vibrant array of hobbies. She regularly visits art galleries, museum exhibitions, and live music venues across Austin and beyond. Photography and creative writing allow her to capture and craft stories inspired by everyday moments. She enjoys cooking experimental dishes, exploring international cuisines, and sharing meals with friends. Outdoor pursuits such as hiking the Texas Hill Country and practicing yoga provide stress relief. Patricia also volunteers at community arts programs, attends professional networking events, and reads contemporary fiction, non‑fiction, and thought‑leadership books.
info.sports_persona: Patricia Horney embraces the Austin outdoors by hiking the Hill Country trails, practicing yoga at Radiant Yoga studio, cheering for Austin FC in MLS games, following the Dallas Cowboys for NFL Sundays, and playing recreational soccer with the Green Army community club, all while they schedule weekly runs to balance stress and maintain fitness.
info.arts_persona: Patricia Horney fuels her creative appetite by frequenting the Blanton Museum of Art, attending installations at the Contemporary Austin gallery, capturing candid street scenes in downtown Austin through photography, and immersing in live performances by Saint Vincent and Alejandro Escovedo, while they draw inspiration from artists like Yoko Ono and Bill Viola to shape their own storytelling projects.
info.travel_persona: Patricia Horney curates a blend of purposeful getaways and spontaneous escapes, favoring weekend retreats to the Texas Hill Country vineyards, extended immersions in Barcelona’s modernist architecture, culinary tours of Marrakech’s souks, and a dream itinerary to Kyoto’s temples, while they budget trips through a dedicated travel fund and often plan itineraries using curated playlists for mood‑setting.
info.culinary_persona: Patricia Horney experiments in the kitchen with global flavors—crafting kimchi‑infused tacos, sous‑vide lamb with rosemary and sumac, and miso‑carbonara ramen—while they juggle an intermediate cooking skill set, source fresh produce from the Austin Farmers’ Market, and host monthly dinner parties where saffron‑perfumed paella leads the menu.

info.persona: Magin Rampersad blends a quiet, routine‑driven discipline with a love for solitary fishing and meticulous cooking, yet can’t resist buying the newest fishing lure each season, even when it’s unnecessary.
info.professional_persona: Magin Rampersad, a seasoned long‑haul truck driver turned logistics mentor, leverages three decades of route‑planning precision, defensive‑driving expertise, and bilingual communication to instill routine‑driven safety and reliability in younger drivers while preparing to transition into fleet management.
info.cultural_background: Magin was born to Mexican immigrants who first settled in Texas before the family relocated to South Carolina when he was a teenager. He grew up bilingual, celebrating Mexican holidays such as Día de los Muertos and Cinco de Mayo while also embracing Southern traditions like church picnics and Southern hospitality. His Mexican heritage informs his cuisine, family values, and close‑knit community orientation, whereas his Southern upbringing contributed to his practical, modest demeanor and respect for routine. This blend of cultures is evident in his bilingual communication style, his love for both Mexican and Southern comfort foods, and his participation in local church and community events.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Magin enjoys solitary activities that align with his calm, routine‑oriented personality. He spends early mornings fishing at Lake Hartwell, tending to a modest vegetable garden behind his home, and perfecting traditional Mexican dishes such as pozole and tamales. He listens to classic rock and regional Mexican music while cooking or gardening. He reads historical biographies and occasionally volunteers at the local community center, teaching basic Spanish to seniors. He attends his church’s small‑group gatherings on Sundays and enjoys walking his Labrador along neighborhood nature trails.
info.sports_persona: Magin Rampersad enjoys low‑impact fitness through early‑morning fishing on Lake Hartwell, weekend walks on the Piedmont Path with his Labrador, and cheering for the Atlanta Falcons and Atlanta Braves, while occasionally joining the Hartwell Trail Runners club for 5K community runs.
info.arts_persona: Magin Rampersad finds solace in classic rock legends like Led Zeppelin and The Rolling Stones, as well as regional Mexican icons such as Vicente Fernández, pairing the music with his gardening and cooking routines, and occasionally attends local church choir performances featuring works by Mozart.
info.travel_persona: Magin Rampersad prefers meticulously planned road trips that balance scenic relaxation with culinary discovery, favoring destinations like the Texas Hill Country for its BBQ and ranch culture, the historic streets of Puebla, Mexico for authentic tamale recipes, and the nearby Blue Ridge Mountains for weekend fishing retreats.
info.culinary_persona: Magin Rampersad, an adept home cook, regularly perfects traditional Mexican dishes such as pozole with hominy, pork shoulder, and dried chilies, and hand‑rolled tamales stuffed with masa, pork, and roasted tomatillos, while also cultivating garden‑grown zucchini, corn, and cilantro to complement his meals.

info.persona: Maria Suarezgonzalez blends quiet curiosity with practical routines, nurturing her garden, crafts, and heritage recipes while quietly mentoring loved ones, all from a relaxed, solitary lifestyle that values harmony over hustle.
info.professional_persona: Maria Suarezgonzalez is a retired home economist who now volunteers at the local community center, teaching cooking and crochet to youth and seniors, leveraging her calm listening skills to mediate small disputes while preferring one‑on‑one, quiet mentorship over large group settings.
info.cultural_background: Maria was raised in a close‑knit Puerto Rican family that settled in the Bronx during the 1960s. Bilingual Spanish‑English at home, she grew up celebrating traditions such as Nochebuena, Three Kings Day, and the vibrant sounds of salsa and plena. The neighborhood’s Puerto Rican churches, festivals, and food markets played a key role in shaping her identity, blending Caribbean warmth with the fast‑paced urban life of New York City. Her cultural values emphasize family loyalty, respect for elders, and the sharing of food as a means of connection. Although she has adapted to American customs, she maintains a strong sense of Caribbean heritage, passing on recipes, stories, and language to the next generation.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Maria finds comfort in solitary pursuits. She spends mornings tending to her container garden, harvesting basil and cilantro for her meals. Afternoons are often dedicated to crocheting blankets that she donates to local shelters. She enjoys reading historical biographies and classic novels, listening to salsa and bolero on headphones, and documenting family stories through audio recordings. Weekly, she attends Mass and joins a small choir, which offers a quiet, reflective space. Occasionally, she explores genealogy websites to trace her Puerto Rican roots, balancing curiosity with the practicality of preserving her heritage.
info.sports_persona: Maria Suarezgonzalez follows the New York Yankees and the New York Knicks on TV, participates in the Golden Years Walking Club that meets thrice weekly at the local park, and practices gentle yoga at home twice a week to maintain flexibility.
info.arts_persona: Maria Suarezgonzalez enjoys listening to classic salsa legends like Celia Cruz and bolero crooner Armando Manzanero on her headphones, attends the local choir’s rehearsal at St. Mary's Church, admires the works of Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera during museum visits, and routinely crochets blankets while the music plays.
info.travel_persona: Maria Suarezgonzalez relishes day trips to historic coastal towns such as St. Augustine, FL, cherishes a past visit to the Caribbean island of Dominica during a family reunion, and dreams of a gentle cruise back to the island of her ancestors, preferring organized tours with her grandchildren and using senior discounts for train travel.
info.culinary_persona: Maria Suarezgonzalez is a master of traditional island staples such as arroz con gandules, alcapurrias, and lechón, expertly seasoning them with her homegrown basil and cilantro, and she enjoys experimenting with a quick‑flash steaming technique for plantains while still honoring the slow‑cooked sofrito base.
